faqs.a:
There shall be, except as hereafter provided, imposed on the alarm user of an alarm
               system for every false alarm to which the police department responds, an administrative
               charge at a rate established by the chief of police, approved by the city manager,
               and as set forth in the administrative fee schedule. A charge shall not be levied
               on the alarm user where it has been defined by the chief of police that such alarm;
(1)
Was valid; or
(2)
Was activated by weather conditions and such alarm could not have been prevented by
                  reasonable precautions; or
(3)
Was intentionally activated with a reasonable belief that criminal activity was occurring
                  or was about to occur; or
(4)
Is installed on residential premises or a public facility on which there have been
                  fewer than four false alarms during the current calendar year. For purposes of this
                  subsection, the "current calendar year" shall begin on the first date subsequent to
                  the effective date of this amendment (August 9, 1983) that the police department responds
                  to a false alarm on said premises or public facility.
(Code 1981, § 2-191(b); Ord. No. 1745, §§ 2—6, 5-18-1981; Ord. No. 1959, § 1, 8-1-1983;
               Ord. No. 3237, § 2, 12-18-1995)
